findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced last week." followed by a `<ul>` containing only 3 `<li>` items
findings.fix: Add the missing 4th project to the list, or change the text to "3 projects."
findings.location: workspace-overview section, "Your projects" paragraph and list
findings.violation: The stated project count doesn't match the number of projects actually listed.

findings.evidence: Workspace list shows "Holiday Campaign Assets," "Support Backlog Triage," "Mobile App Revamp," but `<input id="project-settings-name-input" type="text" value="Q3 Roadmap">`
findings.fix: Rename the settings example to match one of the listed projects, or add "Q3 Roadmap" to the workspace project list.
findings.violation: "Open project settings" is the only path into project settings, yet it leads to a project ("Q3 Roadmap") that never appears anywhere in the workspace's project list, making the mockup's data inconsistent across screens.

findings.fix: Add visible text (e.g., "Duplicate") or an icon to the button's content.
findings.violation: The button has no visible text or icon content, so sighted users see a blank control with no indication of its purpose; the aria-label only helps screen-reader users.

findings.evidence: `project-settings-duplicate-btn` has no href, form association, or corresponding result section anywhere in the document
findings.fix: Link it to a new section demonstrating the duplicated project, or remove it from the mockup.
findings.violation: Unlike every other action in the mockup, this button doesn't lead to any resulting state, making it a non-functional dead end.

findings.evidence: `<form>` elements with `<button type="submit">Save</button>` and no `action` attribute, while all other navigation in the document uses `<a href="#section">` anchors
findings.fix: Give each Save control a defined next state consistent with the anchor-navigation pattern (e.g., navigate to a "Saved" confirmation section), or remove the `<form>`/submit semantics.
findings.violation: Submitting these forms triggers a real page reload/GET request instead of moving to a mockup state, breaking the anchor-based navigation pattern used everywhere else, and there is no confirmation screen for a successful save.

findings.evidence:
`Continue` is separate from the `
` and unconnected to `invite-member-email-input`
findings.fix: Tie navigation to form submission and require a non-empty, valid email before allowing continuation.
findings.violation: Clicking "Continue" navigates straight to "Invite sent" regardless of whether an email address was entered, so an invite can appear sent with no recipient.

findings.evidence: "You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list."
findings.fix: Add an archived-projects-list section with a link from here (and from project-archived), or remove the reference.
findings.violation: No "archived projects list" screen or link exists anywhere in the document, so this text refers to a destination that isn't part of the mockup.

findings.evidence: `Cancel` and `Archive`, both plain unstyled anchors
findings.fix: Style the Archive action distinctly (e.g., as a warning button) to differentiate it from the safe Cancel option.
findings.violation: The destructive "Archive" action is visually indistinguishable from "Cancel," making an accidental archive easy to trigger.

findings.evidence: e.g. `<input id="project-settings-name-input" type="text" value="Q3 Roadmap">` - none of the form controls have a `name` attribute
findings.fix: Add appropriate `name` attributes to each form control.
findings.violation: Without `name` attributes, these fields would not be included in an actual form submission, so "Save" could never function as real form data.
